research_mode: official Department for Transport accredited statistics; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.name: Children casualty shares
verified_claims: People aged 16 or under accounted for 3% of fatalities and 10% of all casualties in 2025.
limitations: Age shares do not indicate risk at a school, home or parcel.

sources.name: Young-adult casualty shares
verified_claims: People aged 17 to 29 accounted for 23% of fatalities and 28% of all casualties in 2025.
limitations: National age-group shares require exposure data before comparison.

sources.name: Older casualty shares
verified_claims: People aged 70 and over accounted for 24% of fatalities and 8% of all casualties in 2025.
limitations: The figures do not control for travel patterns or local population structure.

sources.name: Male fatalities
verified_claims: There were 1,200 male road fatalities in 2025, 2% fewer than 2024 and 9% fewer than 2015.
limitations: Sex-specific national totals are not parcel-level indicators.

sources.name: Female fatalities
verified_claims: There were 356 female road fatalities in 2025, 7% fewer than 2024 and 14% fewer than 2015.
limitations: Small subgroup changes can fluctuate and do not locate incidents.

sources.name: Known missing collisions
verified_claims: Around 100 collisions, including 3 fatalities, were not yet included in the provisional data and were expected in final statistics.
limitations: The provisional totals are incomplete by design.

sources.name: Potential duplicates
verified_claims: The provisional data may contain a small number of duplicate casualty records that will be removed during end-of-year validation.
limitations: Unvalidated records must not be treated as final granular evidence.

sources.name: Vehicle-type misclassification
verified_claims: Some provisional road-user figures can be affected by misclassified vehicle types and later reclassification using police and DVLA information.
limitations: Category-level figures can change after validation.

sources.name: Non-fatal under-reporting
verified_claims: Alternative hospital, survey and compensation data indicate that a considerable proportion of non-fatal casualties are not known to police.
limitations: Police-reported counts should not be presented as the complete incidence burden.

sources.name: Provisional versus final comparison
verified_claims: For 2020 to 2022, national provisional-to-final changes were typically under 1% and did not alter overall trends.
limitations: Small national revisions do not guarantee stability for individual police-force or local-area figures.
